doc.title: John Budd interviewed by Monk Rowe, Aspen, Colorado, October 11, 1997 [transcript only]

title: Classical pianists he admired and meeting Gene Schroeder and Yank Lawson at Condon's
summary: Rachmaninoff, de Pachmann, Cortot, then friends such as Dick Hyman, Dick Wellstood, and first meeting Schroeder and Lawson.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Who played piano: the pianists musicians remembered

blocks.x: It is, yes. People that I admire that I used to listen to, my mother would have me listen to, was Rachmaninoff, hear him play his own things, and hear, a very interesting guy was DePackman, Vladimir DePackman. And he was a great — he loved to play Chopin music. And in those days records were made on wax and disks and so forth, and he’d become so enthralled in the music they tell me that he was playing some Chopin so meditatively, he’d say “oh that sounds so good,” and ruin the record and had to do it over again. And another, Alfred Corteau was a Swiss guy. I never saw him, but I had his records. And Olga Samaroff was a Polish girl who played a marvelous tune called “Sparkputz.” Other musicians tell me it’s a great favorite, a difficult tune. But I learned about those people and of course the other musicians I’ve learned that I’ve liked so much: Dick Hyman has been very good to me, and Dick Wellstood I got to know him, and also he had a big, he almost bled to death after a tonsillectomy one time and his wife was a nurse and was telling me about that so we talked about music in that case. And he’s one and there’s so many. Sajeen Shader was very nice to me, and one of the first I even spoke to when I went to Eddie Condon’s place. After each set played they’d go out and Ralph Sutton was the intermission pianist, and he’d be playing the piano, and the other guys would adjourn to the bar and they’d talk out there. I remember speaking to Shader and I asked “Mr. Shader, I enjoy your piano playing and I’ve heard you on records.” And he was very cordial and “glad to know you” and said “I’m glad you like it. Come in and listen the rest of the night.” So I did. And I saw Yank Lawson there at that time too, and he said “what’s your name?” And I said “John Henry Budd.” And he says “I’m John Henry Lawson.” Then we became friends.
